intent: To demonstrate that the United States tax system is largely flat rather than progressive when all tax types are combined, challenging the common perception that the wealthy pay a significantly higher share of their income.

requirements.question: Should the video be required to convey the overall flat/moderate combined-burden pattern, or is that interpretation optional?
Must the video make the Richest-below-Poorest comparison explicit, or only show overall flatness?
Should income-tax progressivity be included as required context for the contrast, or is it optional background?
Must the video show tax-mix composition differences, or is only the combined total required?

units.claim: Combined tax burden across income groups is only modestly varying and not strongly progressive; it does not rise steadily with income.
accept: Combined taxes stay in a moderate band, roughly 23.7% to 31.5% of income, rather than climbing steeply with income.
The overall tax burden does not rise steadily from poorest to richest; it is relatively flat with only modest variation.
When all tax types are combined, the pattern is not a strong progressive rise.
units.evidence: The total combined tax burden for each income group must be visually comparable across the distribution, at least for Poorest, 5th, 10th, and Richest.

units.claim: The Richest income group's total tax burden is lower than the Poorest group's and lower than the 10th group's; it is the lowest total burden among the listed groups.
accept: Richest pays 23.7% of income in total taxes, below Poorest at 24.1% and far below the 10th group at 31.5%.
The richest group is the lowest total-tax group, not the highest.
The billionaire at the top pays a smaller overall share than everyone else, including the poorest.
units.evidence: The total-tax values for Richest, Poorest, and 10th must be visually comparable so the Richest-lower-than-Poorest and Richest-lower-than-10th relationships can be read.

units.claim: Income taxes alone are progressive across most of the distribution, rising sharply from lower to higher income before the Richest group falls below the 10th group.
accept: Income taxes rise from 1.003% for the 2nd group to 17.998% for the 10th group, then fall to 10.003% for the Richest.
Income taxes look strongly progressive up through the 10th group, but the Richest is lower than the 10th.
The progressive impression comes mainly from income taxes alone, not from all taxes combined.
units.evidence: The income-tax component must be visible or separable enough to show the rise from lower/middle groups to the 10th group and the drop at Richest.

units.claim: The tax mix differs by income: lower-income groups rely mostly on consumption and payroll taxes, while the Richest group relies more on corporate/property and income taxes.

basis.note: Poorest-Consumption taxes share of Poorest tax mix
Poorest-Payroll taxes share of Poorest tax mix
Richest-Corporate and property taxes share of Richest tax mix
Richest-Income taxes share of Richest tax mix
Richest-Consumption taxes share of Richest tax mix
Richest-Payroll taxes share of Richest tax mix

accept: For the Poorest, consumption and payroll taxes are about 51.9% and 44.0% of the tax mix; for the Richest, corporate/property and income taxes are about 44.3% and 42.2%.
Lower-income groups pay mostly through consumption and payroll taxes, while the Richest pays mostly through corporate/property and income taxes.
The composition of taxes shifts from payroll/consumption at the bottom to income/corporate-property at the top.
units.evidence: The tax-type composition for at least Poorest and Richest must be visible so their different shares of the tax mix can be compared.

optional_valid: Payroll taxes are a large but relatively stable percentage of income for most lower/middle groups, e.g. 10.602% for Poorest and 10.399% for 5th, before dropping to 0.397% for Richest.
Estate taxes appear only for the 10th group (0.303% of income) and Richest (0.801% of income) in the table.
Consumption tax burden falls from 12.499% for Poorest to 1.999% for Richest.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded

clip_hardcase.reason: The reference SVG has no explicit data-role=bar mark, so visual-unit reconstruction needs manual review.

hardcases.handling: Requires human visual inspection before semantic scoring.
